A1.justification: Both complete 32-page PDFs describe the same work, Flat Channels to Infinity in Neural Loss Landscapes. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison of the main text, figures, table, equations, references, and Appendices A–C.

before.justification: v2 reports original neural-network simulations, including channel frequencies across regression datasets, loss-landscape analyses, and optimizer trajectories in Figures 2–6, with additional results in the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original simulations and analyses, including the 4,420-network study documented in Appendix B.3 and its reported channel statistics.

M1.justification: Neuron duplication, channel identification, the two-neuron reparameterization, and the jump procedure in Appendix C.1 are unchanged. No model component or algorithmic step is added or revised.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same modified Rosenbrock targets, four Gaussian-process kernel scalings, erf toy regression problem, and ReLU population-loss example. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Figure 6 retains the same gradient-flow, SGD, ADAM, and finite-step GD comparisons. No evaluated comparison method is added, removed, or revised.

E3.justification: Table 1 and Appendices A.2, B.3, and C.4–C.5 retain identical sample sizes, architectures, solver settings, channel-detection thresholds, and optimizer protocols. The finite-data and population-loss evaluation settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: The bias comparisons, perturbation and convergence diagnostics, channel geometry analyses, activation-function examples, and edge-of-stability investigations are retained unchanged, including their appendix evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions report 50 × 2^r simulations per architecture in Appendix A.2 and 50 random initializations per configuration in Appendix B.3. Statistical displays and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Reported numerical values, channel frequencies, plotted trajectories, and qualitative findings in Figures 2–6 and the appendices are unchanged. The graphical revisions affect labels and typography, without changing results.

T1.justification: Equations 1–42 and the accompanying assumptions and derivations are unchanged, including the population-loss calculations, stability analysis of minima at infinity, and higher-derivative constructions in Appendix C.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same claims about channels to infinity, their frequent discovery by gradient-based training, and their limiting implementation of gated linear units.

C2.justification: Interpretations of channel sharpness, generalization, regularization, and optimizer behavior are unchanged. Both versions retain the same qualifications about large-scale applicability, general convergence proofs, and the saddle-line recovery heuristic.

D1.justification: The implementation, hardware, hyperparameter, and data-generation disclosures in Appendices A–C are identical. The code-availability statement and reported repository link in Section 5 are also unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 1.1, the main and appendix reference lists, and the positioning relative to neuron-splitting research and other minima at infinity are unchanged. No cited work is added or removed.

P1.justification: v4 adds an explicit equal-contribution note explaining the existing author asterisks and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The scientific prose and section organization are otherwise identical.

P2.justification: Figure 1 replaces the limiting-weight arrow notation with explicit shared w labels. Figures 1–3 receive small mathematical-label typography changes, and page 1 reflows around the author note. All other pages, including every appendix page, render identically.

improvement.justification: v4 clarifies equal-contribution attribution and makes localized figure-label and layout refinements. The scientific explanations, empirical evidence, theory, reproducibility information, and limitations remain unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. These limited editorial changes do not materially alter the paper's overall quality.
